headline: Southborough boards reviewed plans for a proposed Costco warehouse, advanced a municipal wage overhaul, and revised regional school assessments following state aid increases.
synopsis: The Conservation Commission opened hearings on stormwater and wetland plans for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive. The Personnel Board adopted a 60th percentile salary benchmark for a municipal compensation study and established a November 24 appeal deadline for town employees. Regional school officials re-voted a revised $31.52 million FY27 budget that slightly reduces member town assessments due to increased state Chapter 70 aid. Meanwhile, the Affordable Housing Trust backed a draft senior housing zoning bylaw and confirmed that roughly one million dollars in housing funds were shifted to an interest-bearing account.

highlights.title: Costco warehouse and gas station review opens
highlights.why: Costco presented stormwater and wetland plans for a 167,000-square-foot retail warehouse and 30-position fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive on the site of a demolished office building. The public hearing was continued to November 19 pending consultant peer review and state comments.

highlights.title: Municipal wage study benchmark and appeal process
highlights.why: The Personnel Board voted to adopt a 60th percentile salary benchmark for non-union town staff within a proposed 12-grade structure. Following job ranking concerns from department heads, the board set a November 24 deadline for employees to submit formal reconsideration requests.

highlights.title: Regional school FY27 budget re-vote
highlights.why: The Regional School Committee re-voted the FY27 budget at $31,521,177 after state Chapter 70 funding increased by roughly $104,000. The additional aid lowered Southborough's assessment to $10,731,901 and Northborough's to $17,106,241.

highlights.title: Draft senior housing zoning amendment
highlights.why: The Affordable Housing Trust reached consensus to support draft zoning that allows up to eight units per acre on two-acre parcels for 55-plus housing with a 12.5 percent affordability requirement. The trust plans to present the draft to the Planning Board and Zoning Board of Appeals in late fall.

highlights.title: Housing trust funds moved to interest account
highlights.why: Roughly one million dollars in municipal affordable housing funds previously kept in a zero-interest account were moved into an insured savings program earning about 3.5 percent interest. The shift is projected to generate approximately $35,000 in annual revenue for housing initiatives.
